Which crop shows the described drawing better?

20 pairs. The two crops come from two versions of the layout model in a random order. Pick the better one for the description, then press Export and save the file as grades.json.

p01: mlt_week09_page004 D1

A line through the origin with a point $(\begin{bmatrix}1\\1/2\end{bmatrix},-1)$ on one side labeled $+1$, and $(\begin{bmatrix}-1\\0\end{bmatrix},+1)$, $(\begin{bmatrix}0\\-1\end{bmatrix},+1)$ on the other side.

p02: ie643_lec03_page004 D1

A line $x_1 - 2x_2 = 3$ (offset/bias) plotted on axes $x_1, x_2$, with a point $(x_1, x_2)$ marked near the line, showing its projection onto the normal vector $\vec{n}$ of the line.

p03: ie802_notes_page047 D1

A polygon with a marked corner point, labeled "basic Gom point", and an arrow labeled "cut off here as much deeper".

p04: ie643_lec09_page013 D1

A column of output neurons $\hat{y}_1, \hat{y}_2, \dots, \hat{y}_C$, each connected to a separate box (layer input).

p05: ie643_lec03_page002 D1

A perceptron neuron — inputs $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_d$ each with weight $w_1, w_2, \dots, w_d$, feeding into a dot-product sum $\sum_{j=1}^{d} w_j x_j$. The output branch splits: $\geq\theta \to +1$, $<\theta \to -1$.

p06: ie802_notes_page041 D5

A scatter plot of points with a red separating line, labeled "minimize flat hat 2-norm" — "split cutg..." — "not necessary" — "no good" — "too big of separation" — "using convex hulls" — "shrink" — "and convex hull".

p07: mlt_week09_page003 D1

Two scatter plots of data points with a dashed decision boundary line, showing an initial misclassified point near the origin being corrected by the update rule, resulting in a new, more accurate boundary.

p08: ie643_lec09_page015 D1

A chain of neurons labeled $a_1^L, a_2^L, \dots, a_C^L$, each feeding into the next.

p09: ie802_notes_page052 D1

A wavy curve with a local minimum marked at the start, and another point further along the curve.

p10: ie643_lec07_page008 D1

A wavy curve with an arrow pointing left from a marked point, labeled "step length/learning rate."

p11: ie802_notes_page042 D3

Two separate sets $S_1$ and $S_2$ each with a line $\alpha x \leq \beta$ through them.

p12: ie802_notes_page041 D6

A polygonal region with a red separating line through it, labeled "split cutg..." — "this has been done before" — "(shrinkage needs more research)".

p13: ie802_notes_page042 D1

A set $S$ split into two regions by a vertical line, labeled "S" on the left and "$11$" on the right.

p14: ie802_notes_page041 D2

$S$ and $T$ separated by an arrow, labeled "Separate $S$ from $T$ by a hyperplane... on linear."

p15: ie802_notes_page048 D1

A shaded region with a cut through it, illustrating the idea of traveling 2 sides of a corner point and cutting all the edge of infeasible region then draw a cut.

p16: ie802_notes_page042 D4

An oval region split by a red line into two halves, labeled $R_1$ on the left and a shaded region on the right.

p17: ie643_lec09_page014 D1

A chain of fully-connected layers (left) vs. a fully-connected layer feeding into a single output neuron (right).

p18: mlt_week03_page007 D1

A 2D scatter plot showing two clusters — yellow shaded region labeled "Cluster 1 region" on the left, green shaded region labeled "Cluster 2 region" on the right. A dashed line from $\mu_1$ to $\mu_2$ is shown, with an arrow pointing right labeled "$(x_2-\mu_1)$". The line $x^T(\mu_2-\mu_1)=0$ is marked at the bottom.

p19: ie802_notes_page046 D3
